alt: Four narrowing filters for the non-exam assessment text: a substantial whole prose fiction text, not on the 9275 prescribed list, from the canon of the British Isles or seminal world literature of any period, and similar in challenge to the Paper 1 set texts. Jane Eyre, Frankenstein and Things Fall Apart are given as examples.
caption: A good NEA novel passes every filter and rewards rereading.

alt: A bar splits the NEA’s 20% into AO1 8%, AO2 8% and AO3 4%. A six-step ladder of levels shows Level 1 (1–5 marks) as simple, narrative or descriptive comments, Level 4 (16–20) as clear understanding and Level 6 (26–30) as convincing, critical analysis. From Level 3 up, the descriptors refer to the whole text.
caption: Higher levels need a whole-text, critical response, not a few chapters.

alt: Three weak tasks, such as “Write about the main character”, are each turned into a strong “How does the writer…” or “How far…” task about duty and desire, structure and sympathy, or the ending and belonging. A strong task has a focus, invites an argument and points to the writer’s methods.
caption: Ask how the writer presents something, so the task demands an argument.

alt: A thesis that isolation is both a punishment and a source of self-knowledge leads five sections spread from the beginning to the end of the novel: opening chapters, setting, relationships, turning point and ending, which echoes the opening. Every section combines method analysis (AO2), themes and context (AO1) and an argued voice (AO3), followed by a concluding judgement.
caption: A thesis, five sections from beginning to end, and all three AOs in each.

alt: Four steps in order: write a full first draft, revise for argument, revise for analysis, then edit for accuracy. A note says to keep notes and drafts and record sources so the work can be confirmed as your own.
caption: Fix the argument first, then the analysis, then the accuracy.

alt: A timeline of six stages before the centre’s deadline: reread the novel with the task in mind, gather and organise evidence, write a plan, complete a draft, revise the argument, and do a final accuracy check. An arrow shows planning backwards from the deadline.
caption: Set your dates backwards from the deadline, with time left to revise.
